title: The zines in the window
logline: A bookstore on main street that wasn't there before, and in its window, zines — stapled, quarter-letter, the shape of the laundromat digest. Not his. Somebody's. The page looks at them the way the 2001 customers looked at frames.

panels.composition: A new bookstore's window on main street in August: a display of stapled quarter-letter zines on a stand, hand-lettered covers, none of them his, the shape exactly the laundromat digest's. The street reflected over them. The ridge glow above the roofs in the reflection.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a bookstore window in August displaying a stand of small stapled hand-lettered zines, the street reflected over the glass with a warm glow above the rooftops in the reflection, no people, no words
image.notes: Vol 7's zines. Not his. The digest's shape.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: Someone else's digests, in a window.
